PART 1: NARRATION READY
Your HAD2500 transformer tells a compelling efficiency story that combines excellent electrical infrastructure with substantial waste elimination opportunity. The electromagnetic field analysis reveals textbook voltage stability at 477.8 volts with clean waveform delivery throughout April's monitoring period. You're seeing no voltage stress indicators — no triangular drops, no sustained dips below your nominal 480-volt target — which creates an ideal foundation for optimization. However, beneath this voltage excellence lies significant reactive power stress. Your facility draws 742.2 kVAR maximum during production peaks while maintaining 96.3% power factor. This reactive demand creates 177,167 BTU per hour of waste heat that requires 20.7 kilowatts of cooling capacity, costing approximately $2.34 hourly to remove. The MPTS simulation projects dramatic improvement — eliminating 495.2 kVAR of reactive draw would achieve 99.5% power factor while recovering approximately $684,764 annually in combined waste costs. Based on your reactive demand profile, preliminary sizing suggests approximately two H490 units at roughly $400,000 installed investment. Your consistent five-day production schedule provides excellent predictability for correction system design, while the voltage stability ensures optimal MPTS performance without requiring infrastructure upgrades.

PART 2: EXECUTIVE SHORT
HAD2500 presents an excellent MPTS opportunity combining stable electrical infrastructure with substantial reactive power waste. Your transformer maintains exemplary 477.8-volt delivery with no stress indicators, but draws 742.2 kVAR maximum reactive power that creates significant thermal burden. The facility operates with strong discipline — five-day production schedules with 85% of weekdays above your 1,558.5 kVA target. This operational consistency maximizes MPTS effectiveness. Harmonic content remains controlled at 6.0%, indicating clean equipment behavior despite reactive stress. MPTS correction would eliminate 495.2 kVAR reactive draw, achieving 99.5% power factor with approximately $684,764 annual recovery potential. Preliminary sizing indicates roughly two H490 units at approximately $400,000 installed investment. The combination of excellent voltage health, substantial waste elimination potential, and predictable operational patterns makes HAD2500 an ideal candidate for electromagnetic efficiency optimization. Pricing note: these figures are planning-level estimates, not final quotes. Final installed pricing depends on engineering scope, labor, and site conditions. For planning, estimated installed investment is roughly $582,000 to $787,000.
